prompt: Which of these is one of the most common causes of traffic collisions?
choices: Using low-beam headlights during the day
explanation: Driver distraction, such as using a phone, eating or daydreaming, is one of the most common causes of collisions, along with unsafe speed and failing to yield. The other choices are normal, safe habits.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.83, NJ p.94, CO p.9, IN p.76)

prompt: A police officer is directing traffic at an intersection. Your light is green, but the officer holds up a hand for you to stop. What should you do?
choices: Go ahead, because the green light gives you the right-of-way
Slow down, then go through if the way looks clear
Stop and follow the officer's directions
Honk to show the officer that your light is green
explanation: Directions from a police officer override traffic lights, signs and pavement markings. Stop and do what the officer signals, even when your light is green.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.51, TX p.31)

prompt: Your windshield wipers suddenly stop working in heavy rain, and you can barely see the road. What should you do?
choices: Slow down and get safely off the road as soon as you can
Speed up to get through the storm more quickly
Stop right where you are in your lane
Follow closely behind the taillights of the car ahead of you
explanation: Without wipers you cannot see well enough to keep driving. Slow down gradually, turn on your hazard flashers and pull safely off the road; some handbooks add that you can roll down your side window to see ahead. Stopping in a travel lane or tailgating invites a crash.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g. AL p.77, MN p.89, NJ p.110, NV p.58)

prompt: How much alcohol does a 5-ounce glass of wine contain compared with a 12-ounce can of regular beer?
explanation: A 12-ounce regular beer, a 5-ounce glass of wine and a 1.5-ounce shot of 80-proof liquor each count as one standard drink with about the same amount of alcohol. Switching from beer to wine does not make it safer to drive.
ref: State driver handbooks (e.g. CA p.79, NJ p.117, PA p.38, TX p.64)
